key_insight: The paper introduces a scalable variational inference framework for SDEs driven by Lévy processes by learning a neural tilting (change-of-measure) that makes posterior path inference tractable and accurate for jumps and heavy tails.
problem_solved: Existing Bayesian inference methods for Lévy-driven SDEs are either computationally infeasible at scale (Monte Carlo) or fail to capture jump-driven heavy tails; this work makes principled, scalable posterior inference possible for such models.
method: Formulate a variational objective over continuous-time path measures for Lévy-driven SDEs and derive an evidence lower bound amenable to optimization.
Introduce a neural tilting (learned change-of-measure) that reweights the Lévy jump measure to produce low-variance, expressive variational families capable of modeling jumps and heavy tails.
Train the tilting network end-to-end with Monte Carlo estimators and amortized inference to enable efficient sampling and uncertainty quantification at scale.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical Bayesian tool to model and quantify uncertainty in systems with jumps and extreme events (e.g., finance, climate, safety-critical AI), improving robustness and predictive reliability while remaining computationally tractable.
visual_elements: Illustration comparing diffusion-only SDE paths vs Lévy jump SDE paths (showing rare large jumps).
Pipeline diagram: data → neural tilting network → tilted Lévy measure → variational sampler → ELBO optimization.
Performance chart: predictive tails/quantiles and uncertainty bands vs baseline methods (MC and naive VI).
Icon set: heavy tails, speed/scale (clock/servers), uncertainty quantification (confidence ribbon), and jump events (lightning bolt).
paper_title: Variational Inference for Lévy Process-Driven SDEs via Neural Tilting
paper_authors: Yaman Kindap, Manfred Opper, Benjamin Dupuis, Umut Simsekli, Tolga Birdal
